ideas: Time helps investments grow through compound interest
An emergency fund must come first
Risk: start small and learn gradually

phrases.meaning: grow as fast as prices rise
fund following a whole stock market
make lots of money very fast

model: I think young people should invest, but only after they've saved a small emergency fund. First, time is their biggest advantage. Thanks to compound interest, money invested in your twenties has decades to grow, which means that even small amounts can turn into a lot. On the other hand, money sitting in a savings account often doesn't keep pace with inflation, so it slowly loses value. When I started working, I began putting one million dong a month into an index fund, and after three years it's grown more than I expected. Another reason is that young people can afford to take risks. If the market falls, they have plenty of time to recover, and investing teaches them about money early. Of course, it's important to spread the risk and avoid anything that promises to make you get rich quick, because that usually results in big losses. So overall, saving a little first and then investing regularly is the best way for young people to grow their wealth.
